verdicts.tldr: No test sends a repeated key, so the doubling branch of gnark's AddMixed, reached from bls12381.go:57, never runs under the package's tests
verdicts.details: Under the package's two Go tests, coverage shows the `return p.DoubleMixed(a)` block of G1Jac.AddMixed (g1.go:460.38,462.3) at count 0. Every key comes from a fresh `sk.SetRandom()` in signers()/committee(). The identity-aggregate pair [k, -k] takes the general addition path. A grep for duplicates finds nothing in any of the four files. If a gnark-crypto bump broke that branch, every test would stay green while a committee whose leading keys are equal got mis-aggregated. The reach is narrow: in FastAggregateVerify the branch fires only when the running sum equals the next key, so only for equal leading keys ([pk, pk, ...]); a later duplicate takes the general path. This overlaps #2, and one case `FastAggregateVerify([k1,k1], 2*s1)` closes this half of both, so merge them at assemble. Fix: add a subtest to TestFastAggregateVerify where [pk, pk] verifies against the two-fold signature and fails against the single one.

verdicts.tldr: No test puts the same key twice in excluded, so nothing pins the per-entry subtraction that committees with a twice-sampled absent member depend on
verdicts.details: bls12381.go:91-98 subtracts every 48-byte entry of excluded and drops no duplicate. A committee that carries a member twice needs exactly that when the member is absent from both positions. Nothing pins it: a duplicate grep returns 0 in all four files, committee() draws a fresh random key per member (bls12381_test.go:139), and the .gno vectors use four distinct secret keys (bls12381_test.gno:74). A refactor that deduplicates excluded keys, such as a decoded-key cache keyed by bytes or a reject-duplicates guard, would keep every test green while updates from any such committee stop verifying. The Ethereum source the finder cites (get_next_sync_committee_indices, 'with possible duplicates') was not fetched in this round. The FastAggregateVerify half overlaps #1; the excluded [k2,k2] half belongs to this candidate alone. Fix: add a case where committee {k1,k2,k2,k3} with excluded [k2,k2] and signature s1+s3 verifies, and excluded [k2] does not.

verdicts.tldr: No test pins that the natives reject non-canonical point encodings (x >= p, infinity with a payload, invalid flag bits), for keys or for signatures
verdicts.details: A grep of both test files for modulus, canonical, deserialization or flag bytes finds nothing. The only malformed-point input is 'garbage signature' at :104-109, which flips one byte at index 10. The infinity cases use canonical encodings (`inf.Bytes()`, and vecInfSig 'c0' plus zeros), which decode fine and are then refused by IsInfinity. gnark rejects all of these inputs today: marshal.go:904-905 returns ErrInvalidEncoding for an invalid mask, :917-918 returns ErrInvalidInfinityEncoding for compressed infinity with a nonzero payload, and :961 calls X.SetBytesCanonical. If a bump relaxed any of those checks, the chain would accept encodings that Ethereum clients reject and no test would fail. The reach is limited: the caller's Merkle proof binds the key bytes, so a second encoding of a key fails membership, and the signature is where a second encoding would get through. Fix: add the deserialization_G1 and deserialization_G2 vectors of ethereum/bls12-381-tests to bls12381_test.go as a table.
verdicts.evidence: grep -n -i 'modulus\|canonical\|deserializ\|flag\|0xe0\|0xa0\|0x80' bls12381_test.go bls12381_test.gno: no hit. Read bls12381_test.go:104-108 'bad[10] ^= 0xff'. Read gnark-crypto v0.20.1 ecc/bls12-381/marshal.go:904-905 'if isMaskInvalid(mData) { return 0, ErrInvalidEncoding }', :917-918 infinity payload check, :961 'p.X.SetBytesCanonical'. The finder's topic1 vector run was not rerun, since it needs a file copied into the package.

verdicts.tldr: crypto/bls12381 is missing from both the amd64/arm64 determinism corpus and every node-level txtar, though its gnark sibling bn254 is in both
verdicts.details: At the full PR head, corpus.gno imports ten stdlib packages, bn254 among them with three call sites (261, 267, 269), and has no bls12381. ci-multiarch-determinism.yml runs `for arch in amd64 arm64` on every gnovm/** change. gnark-crypto v0.20.1 ships fp/element_amd64.go, element_arm64.s and element_purego.go for this curve, so arm64 validators get FastAggregateVerify's verdict from code that no job compares. No txtar names bls12381. stdlib_ibc_crypto_determinism.txtar imports bn254, keccak256, merkle and modexp only, and the one gno.land mention is a comment in apphash_crossrealm38_test.go:232. What the user loses: a gnark-crypto bump that diverges on arm64 would split validators by architecture with CI green, and no test runs the native through addpkg, a tx, qeval and a restart. The finder's topic3 run reports identical digests across builds today, so this guards a future bump rather than a present split. #10 repeats the corpus half; file one of them. Fix: add FastAggregateVerify and FastAggregateVerifyExcluding cases built from the bls12381_test.gno vectors to corpus.gno, and a bls12381 call to stdlib_ibc_crypto_determinism.txtar.

verdicts.tldr: No CI job compares fastAggregateVerify's verdict between gnark's amd64 and arm64 field assembly; this is the same gap as the corpus half of #8
verdicts.details: The import list of corpus.gno (lines 12-21) covers bech32, bn254, chacha20, ed25519, keccak256, merkle, modexp, sha256, subtle and adler32, and not crypto/bls12381. The job builds both architectures on ubuntu-latest, and the bls12-381 fp package ships amd64 and arm64 assembly plus a purego fallback. The ADX sub-claim holds, but it is not this PR's: gnark picks its path at runtime (`var supportAdx = cpu.SupportADX`, element_amd64.go:15), so the single amd64 runner covers one of the two amd64 paths for every gnark native, bn254 included. The restart gas pin stdlib_ibc_crypto_determinism.txtar names bn254, keccak256, merkle and modexp in its header and omits bls12381. What the user loses is the same as in #8: a bump that changes the arm64 verdict would split validators by architecture with CI green. This candidate repeats #8's corpus half, so file it once. Fix: the same corpus case, a known-good vector through FastAggregateVerify and FastAggregateVerifyExcluding plus one off-subgroup key.

verdicts.angle: topic: gas and DoS on every path + claims
verdicts.tldr: No test pins which parameter the two BLS gas rows charge per byte on, so an edit that stops pricing the keys stays green
verdicts.details: native_gas_test.go and native_gas_validate_test.go never name bls12381. TestEveryRowValidates only runs validateRow, which checks SizeModExpWork rows (native_gas.go:272) and misuse of that kind in the other slots (:282). A SlopeIdx of 0 or 1 is in range for both natives (3 and 4 params), so a swap does not trigger an index panic either. innerHash has a shape pin at native_gas_test.go:228; the BLS rows have none, and no txtar pins their gas. What the user loses: with :201 at SlopeIdx 0, the charge is computed on the 48-byte aggregate and stays flat whatever the excluded count, while the native's work grows by one decode and subgroup check per excluded key; with :196 at SlopeIdx 1, the charge follows msg and the keys go unpriced. Fix: add a test to native_gas_test.go, modelled on TestInnerHashGasMetersBothOperands, asserting that fastAggregateVerify slopes on param 0 and fastAggregateVerifyExcluding on param 1, with SizeLenBytes and Slope > 0.
verdicts.evidence: Full PR head: grep -c bls12381 gnovm/stdlibs/native_gas_test.go gnovm/stdlibs/native_gas_validate_test.go: 0, 0. native_gas_validate_test.go:85-99 TestEveryRowValidates calls 'validateRow(e, n)' only. native_gas.go:272 'if e.SlopeKind == SizeModExpWork {'. native_gas_test.go:228 'if inner.SlopeKind != SizeLenBytes || inner.SlopeIdx != 0 || inner.Slope == 0 {'. Rows: :196 'SlopeIdx: 0' (pubkeys), :201 'SlopeIdx: 1' (excluded). Mutation not run: read-only judge.
